key_insight: The paper reformulates neural likelihood learning with unnormalized potentials so the training objective becomes strictly convex, improving theory and identifiability for Bayesian inverse problems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reliable way to learn likelihood surrogates for high-dimensional inverse problems in imaging and scientific computing when traditional MCMC or explicit physics models are too costly.
method: Learn a neural likelihood model directly from data instead of specifying the full generative process.
Use unnormalized potentials and absorb normalization into the objective to obtain a strictly convex optimization problem.
Prove that empirical minimizers converge to the true likelihood as sample size increases.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated with numerical experiments on deblurring and a nonlinear PDE-based imaging inverse problem.
watch_item: The framework is theoretically stronger, but practical performance will still depend on network choice, optimization stability, and how well the data cover the inverse problem’s parameter space.
paper_title: A Convex Approximation Framework for Neural Likelihood-Based Bayesian Inverse Problems
